mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the housing starts (HOUST) exceed 580,000 units in the prior month, it signals strong consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST exceeds 580.0 in 3 consecutive months but the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in UNRATE and increase in PAYEMS occurs in 3 consecutive months but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220), a rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% triggers a monetary tightening cycle that initially suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL > 220.0, a rise in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% does not lead to negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) over the past month signals robust consumer spending, which typically boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases in 3 consecutive months but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 9.5% in the prior month, it indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to higher wage growth and corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 9.5% in 3 consecutive months but the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic expansion, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO and HOUST both increase in 3 consecutive months but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 0.2% in the prior month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 0.2 in 3 consecutive months but the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of those periods.
